Course Registration Process, as per the dates given in the Academic Calendar. Every student
is responsible for his/her registration and completion of registration, failing which he/she shall
not be permitted to attend any classes or use University facilities.
Adding/Dropping Courses: A student may add or drop from the registered elective/audit
courses within a pre-specified period from the commencement of a regular semester, subject
to the availability of resources and the minimum/maximum number of credits required to be
registered in a semester. Final registration for that semester will reflect enrolled courses after
the add/drop date. The courses thus dropped will not appear in the semester Grade Sheet of
the student. However, backlog courses registered during a particular semester cannot be
dropped. While exercising the Add/Drop option, the student may lose attendance in those
courses added during the add/drop period. This issue must be resolved between the course
instructor, the student, and the Faculty Mentor.
Only those electives shall be offered in which the minimum number of registered students
are either 10% of the total strength of the programme or five students, whichever is higher.

rows: The library stands as the intellectual hub of the University, supporting its core missions of teaching,
learning, and research. It serves the information needs of students, faculty, staff, and research
scholars, and is a source of pride for the University. Situated in a fully air-conditioned building, the
library features a spacious, well-furnished reading room that fosters a serene environment and
The library offers a rich collection of resources, including a wide variety of print materials (books,
journals, magazines, project reports, annual reports, newspapers, articles, and case studies) and
electronic resources such as ProQuest, ScienceDirect, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, Sage Online, JSTOR,
Emerald eJournals, HeinOnline, Manupatra, LexisNexis, SCC Online, Wolters Kluwer Arbitration, AIR
Online, LiveLaw, Euromonitor Passport, Economic & Political Weekly, EPWRF India Time Series,
Taxmann, Edzter Magazines & Newspapers and Turnitin. These resources cater to both students
and faculty for research and reference purposes.
Additionally, the library holds institutional memberships with the Developing Library Network
(DELNET) and the National Digital Library of India (NDLI), facilitating resource sharing and access
to an extensive network of academic libraries.
Leveraging Information and Communication Technology (ICT), the library ensures that resources
are accessible 24/7. The Digital Library offers a user-centered environment for scholarly inquiry,
providing services to help users discover and evaluate academic information. It is equipped with
high-speed internet and an intranet network, and all library functions are fully automated, including
the use of smart ID cards and an Online Public Access Catalogue (http://library.bmu.edu.in/),
allowing users to check book availability at any time.
The library provides a range of specialized services, such as Current Awareness Services (CAS),
Selective Dissemination of Information (SDI), News Alerts, Reference Services, Digital
Archiving, and access to the OPAC. Furthermore, it features Knimbus, a remote access tool and
unified search platform, enabling users to access all available resources—both physical and
digital—on a single platform and to retrieve relevant information as needed.
